name: Khalil Center
mission: Khalil Center is a psychological and spiritual community wellness center advancing the professional practice of psychology rooted in Islamic principles. An initiative designed to address the widespread prevalence of social, psychological, familial, relational and spiritual issues of Muslim communities.
theoryOfChange: Khalil Center utilizes a therapeutic framework called "Traditional Islamically Integrated Psychotherapy (TIIP)". This framework is described as an ever-evolving modality of psychological treatment that integrates Islamic principles with modern psychological practices. The TIIP model offers a framework for integrating contemporary behavioral science into an inherently Islamic framework, rooted in an Islamic epistemological and ontological framework. The overarching goals of the TIIP psychotherapeutic encounter include Inkishāf (introspective self-discovery), Inqiyād (engendering treatment compliance & motivation), I'tidāl (equilibrium in all aspects of life), and Ittiḥād (holistic integration). Interventions within this framework are designed to utilize these principles and specifically target the elements of the human psyche: ʿaql (cognition), nafs (behavioral inclinations), rūḥ (spirit), and iḥsās (emotions). This detailed approach to how their programs create impact is outlined on their website, particularly on the "School of Islamic Psychology" page and the "TIIP Certification" page, and is also discussed in their "Our Model of Care" section on the "Mental Health Services" page.

strengths_deep_dive: Khalil Center's primary operational strength lies in its specialized service model and demonstrated clinical effectiveness. Rather than offering generic counseling, the center utilizes Traditional Islamically Integrated Psychotherapy (TIIP). This approach is supported by rigorous empirical validation, including <cite id="6">published outcome data in an APA journal showing substantial reduction in psychological distress</cite>. To expand community capacity, the organization has also <cite id="4">trained over 500 students and mental health professionals</cite> in this framework.

From a financial management perspective, the organization maximizes direct gift application by keeping donor acquisition costs extremely low. Filing data indicates <cite id="1">fundraising costs of just $0.03 per $1 raised</cite>. Furthermore, its zakat program directly addresses healthcare access, providing <cite id="5">11,386 subsidized therapy sessions</cite> to individuals who cannot afford mental healthcare.
rich_narrative.summary: Khalil Center provides faith-based mental health services and clinical training tailored for the Muslim community. In FY2024, the organization recorded <cite id="3">Total Revenue of $2,505,061</cite> to support its clinical programs, community education, and research efforts. The organization operates as a <cite id="2">ZAKAT-ELIGIBLE charity</cite>, using dedicated zakat funds to support lower-income individuals through <cite id="5">11,386 subsidized therapy sessions</cite> in recent operations. Its clinical model integrates modern psychological practices with traditional Islamic spirituality, backed by <cite id="6">published research showing significant reductions in psychological distress</cite>. In FY2024, Khalil Center maintained a <cite id="1">70.1% program expense ratio</cite>, allocating the remaining portion to administrative and operational infrastructure. While this ratio falls below the <cite id="1">75% sector benchmark</cite> and the <cite id="1">87.7% peer median</cite>, the organization demonstrates exceptional fundraising efficiency, spending <cite id="1">only $0.01 to raise every $1</cite>.
